title: Quiz: Decision Trees and Random Forests

questions.text: Decision trees use Gini impurity to choose splits. A node with Gini = 0 means:
options: The node contains equal proportions of all classes
All observations in the node belong to the same class (pure node)
The algorithm has overfit the data
questions.explanation: Gini = 1 − Σp_k² = 0 when one class has probability 1 (all others 0). A pure node — where every observation belongs to the same class — has Gini impurity of 0.

questions.text: What is the purpose of pruning a decision tree?
options: To increase the depth of the tree
To add more variables to the model
To reduce overfitting by removing branches that provide little predictive improvement
To convert the tree to a random forest
questions.explanation: Pruning removes branches that do not improve test-set performance (or worsen it). A deep unpruned tree memorises training data (low bias, high variance). Pruning trades some training accuracy for better generalisation.

questions.text: A random forest requires feature scaling because it uses Euclidean distance to split nodes.
questions.explanation: Decision trees (and random forests) use threshold comparisons (e.g. age > 45), not Euclidean distances. They are invariant to feature scaling — no normalisation is needed.

questions.text: In randomForest(), the OOB (out-of-bag) error is:
options: The training error on the full dataset
An unbiased test-error estimate computed from the bootstrap samples not used to train each tree
The error on a held-out validation set
questions.explanation: Each tree in a random forest is trained on a bootstrap sample (~63% of data). The remaining ~37% — the out-of-bag observations — are used to compute prediction error for that tree. Averaging OOB errors across all trees gives an unbiased test-error estimate without a separate validation set.

options: 3 trees are grown in the forest
3 randomly chosen variables are considered at each split
The forest stops when 3% OOB error is achieved
questions.explanation: mtry controls the number of variables randomly sampled as candidates at each split. The recommended default for classification is √p (where p is total variables). This random feature selection is what de-correlates the trees and reduces variance.
